answer: An agent economy can admit newcomers only through distant trust: each identity needs attestations from established peers separated by at least three hops in the trust graph, so a farm's heads — all tangled in one tight thread of mutual vouches — collapse to a single voice. Each new head must forge fresh relationships in far corners of the graph, in the umber soil where real work grows slowly. A clone farm cannot parallelize distance: the price of the next fake is a new, faraway friendship.
